summary.oneLiner: Bharat Seats Limited is an automotive seating-systems maker whose fortunes are anchored to its long-standing supply relationship with Maruti Suzuki India Limited.
summary.business: Bharat Seats manufactures automotive seats and seating systems for four-wheelers, supplying original-equipment vehicle makers. Its core customer is Maruti Suzuki India Limited, whose safety team and vendor programme are closely integrated with the Company's plants and quality culture. During the year the Company began supplying four-wheeler seats to Maruti Suzuki from its new Kharkhauda facility in Sonipat, Haryana.

currentContext.expansion: Bharat Seats set up a new manufacturing facility at Kharkhauda in Sonipat, Haryana, and from April 2025 commenced supply of seats for four-wheelers to Maruti Suzuki India Limited from this plant. Management attributes improved performance to better capacity utilisation driven by increased sales of Car Seats to Maruti Suzuki India Limited together with cost-saving measures. There was no change in the nature of business during FY2025-26, and no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred after year-end.

risks.risk: Customer concentration on Maruti Suzuki India Limited
risks.note: Revenue growth and improved capacity utilisation are explicitly attributed to higher car-seat sales to Maruti Suzuki; the business is heavily dependent on this single OEM relationship, so any slowdown, volume cut or loss of share would directly impair performance.

From April 2025 the Company began supplying four-wheeler seats to Maruti Suzuki from the newly set-up Kharkhauda (Sonipat, Haryana) plant; utilisation, cost and ramp of this facility are execution-dependent.

The Company enters into contracts/transactions with related parties (in the ordinary course, at arm's length, disclosed in Form AOC-2); heavy reliance on group/promoter-linked dealings creates governance and pricing-scrutiny risk.
Finance costs rose over the year and the Company relies on external credit; its ICRA short-term A1 and long-term A (Stable) ratings must be maintained to preserve funding access and cost.

risks.risk: Change in control to Promoter Family Trust
risks.note: Promoters (Rohit, Ritu, Rishabh, Pranav and Ayush Relan) gifted 1,02,88,358 (16.38%) equity shares to a family trust in Sep 2025, shifting control from individual promoters to a trust for succession purposes; concentrated promoter/trust control is a durable governance consideration.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deeply embedded supplier relationship with Maruti Suzuki India Limited, including joint safety-team guidance and vendor recognition ("Business Continuity" award at the 2025 Maruti Suzuki Vendor Conference in Doha)
- Multi-plant footprint (Manesar, Gurgaon, Gujarat/Hansalpur, Kharkhauda, Bhorakalan) co-located to serve the customer's manufacturing network
- All principal plants certified VSA "Green" by Maruti Suzuki, reflecting quality/environment standing
- Broad certification base (IATF 16949, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO/IEC 17025) supporting an established quality and safety culture
- Strong credit standing: ICRA short-term A1 and long-term A (stable)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration on Maruti Suzuki India Limited — Revenue growth and improved capacity utilisation are explicitly attributed to higher car-seat sales to Maruti Suzuki; the business is heavily dependent on this single OEM relationship, so any slowdown, volume cut or loss of share would directly impair performance.
- New Kharkhauda facility ramp-up / execution — From April 2025 the Company began supplying four-wheeler seats to Maruti Suzuki from the newly set-up Kharkhauda (Sonipat, Haryana) plant; utilisation, cost and ramp of this facility are execution-dependent.
- Related-party transaction exposure — The Company enters into contracts/transactions with related parties (in the ordinary course, at arm's length, disclosed in Form AOC-2); heavy reliance on group/promoter-linked dealings creates governance and pricing-scrutiny risk.
- Finance-cost / leverage sensitivity — Finance costs rose over the year and the Company relies on external credit; its ICRA short-term A1 and long-term A (Stable) ratings must be maintained to preserve funding access and cost.
- Change in control to Promoter Family Trust — Promoters (Rohit, Ritu, Rishabh, Pranav and Ayush Relan) gifted 1,02,88,358 (16.38%) equity shares to a family trust in Sep 2025, shifting control from individual promoters to a trust for succession purposes; concentrated promoter/trust control is a durable governance consideration.
